claims.text: Both physics and theology are circular systems; neither side gets the high ground.
claims.reviewer_notes: Central framing claim of the series; sets up the playing field.

claims.text: Fifteen predictions forward, ten gaps backward — twenty-five data points all pointing the same direction.
claims.reviewer_notes: Core evidence claim; needs verification in chapter 02.

claims.text: The reason inside our heads matches the reason outside in the cosmos; Wigner called it a miracle, founders of physics called it God.
claims.reviewer_notes: Interesting but relies on interpretation of historical figures; needs sourcing.

claims.text: Thirteen paradigm-level replacements in five hundred years; science does not accumulate truth but converges toward a structure it is discovering.
claims.reviewer_notes: Strong claim about scientific progress; needs evidence for the count and interpretation.

claims.text: Every human runs a moral evaluator they did not build, cannot uninstall, and cannot override; that is firmware, not culture.
claims.reviewer_notes: Central claim for chapter 05; strong but needs empirical support.

claims.text: Evil is parasitic; it borrows every word from good and inverts it. The substrate is truthful; the noise came second.
claims.reviewer_notes: Philosophical claim about the nature of evil; needs argumentation.

claims.text: The series provides a scorecard, honest weakness, and kill conditions; the reader can run it themselves.
claims.reviewer_notes: Meta-claim about the series methodology; foundational to the project's transparency.
